Commentary: Ollie Robinson to Shan Masood, no run, full on the pads, Shan Masood gets forward to flick to mid-wicket
Gus Atkinson to Azan Awais, 1 run, short of length outside off, Azan Awais drops it with soft hands in front of backward point and Shan Masood responds
Gus Atkinson to Shan Masood, no run, over the wicket to Shan Masood. A rising short of length delivery outside off, Masood played that well, goes on the back foot and drops it down to backward point
Gus Atkinson to Shan Masood, 1 run, back of a length outside off, Shan Masood goes on the back foot to cut, mistimes it but it's into the gap at cover

Gus Atkinson to Azan Awais, FOUR, round the wicket to Azan Awais and the batter is lucky. It's a sharp nipbacker from a short of length, Awais looks to push and the thick inside-edge runs away well wide of Cox to his right. That could've gone anywhere

16:55 Local Time, 15:55 GMT, 21:25 IST: Rain has come much to Pakistan's relief. Shan Masood walking off with his bat tucked inside his jumper and shirt while Azan Awais is happy to have the bat unguarded. Rain was predicted for 5pm local and it has duly arrived. Tricky conditions for batting and England players loiter around near the boundary before going in. These two batters have weathered the storm after a double-wicket maiden from Robinson to start the innings. Let's hope this rain delay is not a longish one.
The pitch covered with the hover-cover.

17:01 Local Time, 16:01 GMT, 21:31 IST: And that was not a big delay. Covers off and the stumps are being erected. Shan Masood doesn't look too happy as there's a drizzle in the air. Chris Gaffaney has his sunglasses on the top of his white cap. He is opening his eyes wide to get used to the light. Azan Awais takes strike as Atkinson comes from round the wicket with three slips and a gully.
Gus Atkinson to Azan Awais, no run, back of a length on middle, Azan Awais goes on the back foot to turn it to mid-wicket
Gus Atkinson to Azan Awais, no run, full and angled in on off-stump, a solid forward defence back to Gus Atkinson
Jofra Archer [3.0-0-18-0] is back into the attack

Jofra Archer to Shan Masood, FOUR, nice tuck off the hips as Jofra Archer smiles wryly at the sub fielder. It's a good length delivery on leg-stump, Shan Masood goes on the back foot and tucks, the sub fielder at square-leg chases but the ball wins
Jofra Archer to Shan Masood, no run, short of length and just outside off, Shan Masood goes on the back foot and defends it back to Jofra Archer
Rain again. Steady for now.
Jofra Archer to Shan Masood, no run, short around off, Shan Masood goes on the back foot to pull and he finds mid-wicket. Didn't time that
We will be off soon. A matter of when.
Jofra Archer to Shan Masood, 2 runs, full on middle, Shan Masood gets forward to flick and he has timed that between mid-wicket and mid-on for two

17:07 Local Time, 16:07 GMT, 21:37 IST: And off we go. The hover-cover back on. It is getting heavier as I type. The playing square covered. Let's see how long this delay will be. Brollies up in the crowd as a few head for the covered areas. A couple in the crowd enjoying a biscuit, snacks and a pint.

17:12 Local Time, 16:12 GMT, 21:42 IST: The surrounding areas besides the hover-cover has been covered as well. Ian Ward on air tells us that we should be back to play by 6:08pm local or else it will be stumps. Still time left. Hang on for more updates.
Sharath J: Please, Pakistan, at least in the final innings of the tour, show some fight. As a hardcore Test cricket fan, it is disappointing to see matches without any application and fight.
Josh Tongue to Shan Masood, no run, 136ks good length ball close to off, Masood blocks it with a straight bat
Josh Tongue to Shan Masood, 1 run, 138ks sliding down leg, Masood helps it along to fine leg and Archer quickly tidies up

Josh Tongue to Azan Awais, 1 run, 138ks short and well-directed, but Awais plays it really well - rolls his wrists over and pulls backward of square. It was just below the shoulder and hence Awais could control the shot

Josh Tongue to Shan Masood, 1 run, now Masood plays the pull along the ground. He picks it from around off, rides the bounce and sends it to the right of Archer at fine leg. The pace and bounce is not there to trouble the batters..

Josh Tongue to Azan Awais, FOUR, lovely shot! Just a push and the ball race away. Full and outside off, Awais transfers his weight forward, opens the bat face and eases it square of the wicket. Once the ball beat the diving point fielder, there was no stopping that
Gus Atkinson to Shan Masood, no run, 138ks on a length and close to off, Masood meets it on top of the bounce and knocks it to mid-on

Gus Atkinson to Shan Masood, 1 run, that was a tight single. Masood plays it with soft hands in front of mid-on and sets off. Robinson swoops down and scores a direct-hit at the non-striker's end. But Masood was comfortably in..

Gus Atkinson to Azan Awais, 3 runs, good length ball outside off, Awais waits for the ball to come and plays it late, opens the bat face and guides it behind square on the off-side. Gay and Lawrence combine to save a run
Gus Atkinson to Shan Masood, no run, 136ks on a length and in the channel, Masood defends with soft hands and the outside-edge dies down well in front of gully

Gus Atkinson to Shan Masood, FOUR, shot! Runs are starting to flow now.. There are not too many demons in the pitch. The ball is doing less and there are scoring opportunities. This is short and outside off, Masood gets on top and cracks it square of the wicket. No need to run for that..
Gus Atkinson to Shan Masood, no run, 140ks full and angled in, Masood eases it with a straight bat to mid-on
Spin for the first time by England in this Test. It is going to be Lawrence.. Slip and leg slip in place
Dan Lawrence, right-arm off break, comes into the attack
Lawrence to Azan Awais, no run, 85kph, full delivery form round the wicket and the left-hander defends off the front foot

England review! That was quick from Root. The appeal was not confident from Lawrence or Jordan Cox. But Root, standing at leg slip, sends it up immediately, no chat or discussion with the others. It is for a strangle down leg. Did Awais get some bat on the missed glance? Or did it brush his pad? There's a spike when ball is next to the bat. OUT
Dan Lawrence to Azan Awais, THATS OUT!! Caught!!

Dan Lawrence to Azan Awais, out Caught by Jordan Cox!! What a review! Full credit to Root. First for the bowling change. The pacers seemed unlikely to break this partnership, so he brings on the part-time spinner and Lawrence strikes with his second ball. The best part was Root was confident about the appeal, didn't consult Cox or Lawrence before challenging the onfield call. Sliding down leg, Awais prods forward and tries to tickle it into the leg-side, gets a feather on the way to the keeper. Cox collected it cleanly and didn't go up straightaway, Lawrence too just joined in but Root was confident. UltraEdge showed a small murmur when ball was next to the bat. Azan Awais c Jordan Cox b Dan Lawrence 59(84) [4s-10]

Josh Tongue to Babar Azam, 1 run, to point
Josh Tongue to Shan Masood, no run

Josh Tongue to Shan Masood, no run, ufff! He's got that to leave the left-hander. Even Masood went uhhh.
